sources.entry: PitchTap - Open-source menu bar app that changes the key of any app's audio live without changing the tempo. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/gkudva96/pitchtap) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: PitchTap is a free, open-source macOS menu-bar app that changes the key of audio from any app (or all system audio) live, without changing the tempo.
summary.what_it_does: PitchTap captures the audio of one selected app or all system audio using a Core Audio process tap, shifts its pitch in semitones (-12 to +12) plus fine tuning in cents (-50 to +50), and plays the result to the current output device. The original sound is muted while it is on, and the tempo stays the same. It offers tuning presets (A = 440 Hz, A = 432 Hz, and A = 442 to 440), a capo/retuning hint for fretted instruments, and an Original/Shifted toggle for before-and-after comparison. Global keyboard shortcuts control up/down steps, bypass, and reset. The app remembers a chosen app source and resumes shifting when that app plays again. Updates are delivered through Sparkle, and the README says processing is local with nothing recorded or sent.
use_cases: Transpose a song to sing along or karaoke in your vocal range
Change the key of Spotify or Apple Music playback on a Mac
Play along with recordings by matching a song to your instrument's tuning
Shift pitch of a YouTube video or video call audio
Make a song easier to play on guitar or ukulele with a capo-style chord shape
how_to_run: Download PitchTap.zip from the latest release and drag PitchTap into Applications
Open PitchTap; if macOS blocks it, use System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway
Switch PitchTap on and click Allow for system audio access
Build from source: install Xcode command-line tools (xcode-select --install)
notable: Changes key without changing tempo, processing audio live as it plays
Per-app or whole-system audio source selection
Global keyboard shortcuts that work from any app
Capo and retuning guidance for fretted instruments
Self-updating via Sparkle with EdDSA-signed releases
caveats: Requires Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14.4 or newer
Release builds are not signed with a paid Apple developer certificate, so macOS shows a warning and needs an Open Anyway step
Adds about 0.15 s of audio delay, which may show as lip-sync issues in videos
